newsitem.title: POLAND: Flood fear eases in Poland as weekend rain less.
newsitem.headline: Flood fear eases in Poland as weekend rain less.

text.p: Fears of new floods in southern Poland eased on Monday as weekend rain proved less heavy than expected, officials said.

"Despite rains on Sunday and on Monday, the situation is much better than it was and everything suggests it will improve," the spokesman of Poland's flood crisis committee, Krzysztof Pomes, told Reuters. "Water levels are tending to subside on most rivers," he said.
Some areas in southwestern and southern Poland remained under water with more that 1,000 towns and villages touched by the worst flood in centuries. The death toll was 50 people.

Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski is increasingly unlikely to declare a state of emergency in the damaged areas, which would postpone general elections scheduled for September 21, his spokesman said on Monday.
"The final decision has not been taken. But there are less and less circumstances that could compel the president to impose the measure," Antoni Styrczula said.
Pomes said the first flood wave on the Odra river running along the German border was approaching the northwestern port of Szczecin, but was unlikely to swamp the city.
Pomes said new dangers faced the flood-hit major southwestern city of Wroclaw, where lack of clean water prompted fears of an epidemic of dysentery and salmonella among the 650,000 people.
The weekend rain raised water levels in many small mountain rivers in the Nowy Sacz and Jelenia Gora provinces, where floods may still hit several towns and villages, private Radio Zet reported.
